translation_notes: the whole method is one `@graph` declaration plus three islands: `@graph self.__adb_col_statements` names the graph once and the three operations lose their receiver -- `-{ {subject} {self.adb_col_uri} ?o }` (wildcard on the object, the `None` of `remove((s, p, None))`), `bool(m{ ... })` for the `(s, p, None) in g` membership test, `+{ ... {adb_col} }` for the add. This is the clearest before/after of the batch, hence article_candidate

CONFIRMED CAPABILITY, wider than the reference: `@graph` accepts an ATTRIBUTE reference, not only a bare name -- `@graph self.__adb_col_statements` transpiles to `_ldpy_g1 = (self.__adb_col_statements)`. current-graph.md only documents `@graph g` as "the existing Python variable g"; the lexical rule reserves `@graph` followed by `.attr` for the decorator reading, and `@graph self.x` is unambiguous. Worth stating in the reference, because the corpus keeps its graph on `self`

no @prefix is needed: the predicate is `self.adb_col_uri`, an instance attribute set in ArangoRDF.__init__, so it stays an interpolation. Turning it into `<http://www.arangodb.com/collection>` would hard-code what the original reads from the object
`Literal(adb_col)` -> `{adb_col}`: a plain str in object position coerces to a plain Literal (coercion.md), the same term
the docstring is kept verbatim, including `URIRef("http://www.arangodb.com/collection")` inside it -- ldpy never looks inside strings, and the mechanical draft had wrongly rewritten it to `<...>`

context shim (identical for both sides, excluded from the surface metrics): arango_rdf.typings is stubbed (only RDFTerm is used, as an annotation) and ArangoRDFStub carries the two attributes the region touches. The method is extracted as a top-level function, so `self.__adb_col_statements` is NOT name-mangled and the attribute is literally "__adb_col_statements" (the shim sets it with setattr). ArangoRDFStub.__eq__ is the oracle, not original behaviour: the harness compares argument 0 of the two runs, and two graphs built in two namespaces are equal only up to isomorphism

driver: four calls covering the three branches (add on an empty graph, early return when a statement exists, overwrite over two competing statements, overwrite with a neighbouring predicate and a neighbouring subject that must survive). Mutation-checked: replacing `?o` by `{adb_col}` in `-{ }` leaves the stale statements and the driver reports it; so does dropping the membership test

repair.driver: 8 calls added (12 in all): S with a neighbour on another predicate and another subject holding a collection statement but S none (add expected), overwrite on an empty graph, overwrite with the same value, BNode subject (no overwrite / already there / overwrite, next to another BNode), empty collection name, Literal subject; docstring explains each and the one case left out (None).
mutants_killed: existence test widened to any predicate (m{ {subject} ?p ?o })
existence test widened to any subject
object of the added triple as URIRef
removal restricted to the added value
repair.remaining: subject=None: the repository reaches it (rdf_graph.value(s, RDF.object) of a reification missing rdf:object, main.py:3641, 3735, 3820, always overwrite=True) but there the ORIGINAL wipes every adb:collection statement and raises AssertionError ("Subject None must be an rdflib term", from Graph.add), so no run that completes differs; the translation writes Literal('None') as subject, silently, and removes nothing. Verified by execution on both artefacts. It is the known `{expr}`-is-None gap of the language (not expressible without a guard that the original does not have); not in the driver. Article: the example stays publishable (3 islands + @graph against remove/in/add), but only with this footnote; the equivalence holds for every subject that is an rdflib term, and for None the original aborts.

optimization_notes: optimized.py: nothing to compress beyond two blank lines: remove-or-test-then-add on an attribute graph is already minimal (a local alias for the graph would cost as much as it saves).

optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: as the translation, `@graph self.__adb_col_statements`, `-{ ... ?o }` for the wildcard remove, `+{ }` for the add, and the existence test `elif m{ ... }:` without the translation's redundant `bool(...)`. No exception to the symmetry rule.
